 From unimaginable hardships to Asian Para Games glory: Meet the athletes changing India’s sporting story 
 India has started to race away towards the 100 medal mark and the stories coming out of the Asian Para Games are simply mind blowing. This piece is all about some of these athletes whose stories will just humble you.
 Take Pradeep Kumar. He had just been married and was in his village in 2004 when he saw a group of men sexually harassing a woman. He went to stop them and was fired at twice. Two bullets into his spinal chord. Since then he was confined to a wheelchair for 10 years before he discovered para sport. And now he is the winner of back to back Para Asian Games medals for India. Pradeep has a life and a mission. And he is a role model in his village.
 Ram Ratan Singh- In 2017 he suffered a bus accident that left him paralysed below the waist. For some years people said to him he should die. In his words, “They asked me why am I even alive? My life has no purpose and it is much better that I die for I am a burden on everyone. It was the hardest period of my life. A former wrestler who also worked as a delivery boy, he then started para sport and today is a para Asian Games medallist for India.
 Payal Nag- She is the world’s first quadruple amputee archer. For years people said to her she is of no use to anyone and is a burden to her family. Payal and her coach Abhilasha Kumar thought otherwise. Yesterday in Nagoya, Payal, together with Sheetal Devi, won India a silver medal. In her debut Asian Para Games she is a silver medallist and needless to day her life will soon change for the better.
 There are three more days remaining and I have every reason to believe that India will touch that elusive 100 medal mark. Currently in the fourth place in the medal standings with 14 gold, chances are India will also cross the 25 gold medal mark, which they had set out to achieve. Later today I am expecting a flurry of finals in badminton with Pramod Bhagat, Suhas Yathiraj and Nitesh Kumar all in action. Eyes will also be on Sheetal Devi who will be playing her singles gold medal match not to forget Swai Chaudhary in archery.

 Simran Sharma strikes gold, debutant Tejalben Damor gets bronze in Para Asiad's women's 200m T12 eve... 
 In all, this has been a fantastic Para Asian Games so far. And has set the stage for some serious push going forward. There is now reason to believe that India can push for 40 medals in LA28 and also make the top 15 in the world in the medals tally. To do this we need to ensure that the structural transformations continue and para sport continues to be given priority. And if that happens, we will have some more fantastic stories to tell from LA28 each with a potential to transform the country for the better.
 Boria Majumdar is an eminent sports historian, journalist, and writer. He is the founder and editor-in-chief of Revsportz.
